### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Neovim version

0.11 (!at least latest Nightly build!)

### Description

With the default `search_method` of `cover_or_next` and `n_lines` of `50`, mini.ai is sometimes not able to find the `cover` region and falls back to `next`. See reproduction example for more details.

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

```lua
vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim', mini_path }
vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
require('mini.deps').setup()
require('mini.deps').add('echasnovski/mini.ai')
require('mini.ai').setup()
```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Create test.lua as per the following code block below and edit it with `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim test.lua`:
```lua
local M = {
    test = {
        test2 = { "test3" }
    }
}
```


5. Place cursor anywhere on the text `test2`, run `va{`.

6. With the default `search_method` of `cover_or_next`, I would expect `va{` to select the entire
```lua
{
    test2 = { "test3" }
}
```
cover region because it is within the default config of 50 `n_lines`. However, it falls back to `next` region and only selects `{ "test3" }`.

7. Checking default nvim behavior, running the same test with `nvim -u NONE test.lua` shows that `va{` should indeed cover the entire `test` value.

### Note
The doc's known issues section contains the following section for builtin text objects: 
> Certain amount of false positives is to be expected.

However, I'm not sure if this case would fall under this category and I think it's reasonable to expect the command to `cover` in this case.

comment_data.body:
Thanks for the issue!

This is an intended behavior with the default 'cover_or_next' search method. It first [searches in current line](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/fcf982a66df4c9e7ebb31a6a01c604caee2cd488/doc/mini-ai.txt#L453-L455) and only then tries to search in the neighborhood. As there is `next` in the current line, it first prefers it.

To always select covering textobject, set `config.search_method = 'cover'` and use `in` / `an` / `il` / `al` keys to search "next" and "last" textobjects.

Closing as working as expected.

Got it, thanks! I think I still prefer the behavior of `cover_or_next` in the vast majority of cases so I will just continue to use that and keep this behavior in mind.

> It first [searches in current line](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/fcf982a66df4c9e7ebb31a6a01c604caee2cd488/doc/mini-ai.txt#L453-L455) and only then tries to search in the neighborhood. As there is next in the current line, it first prefers it.

Would you consider adding a config option that forces mini.ai to only search in the entire neighborhood by default, and if no cover region is found in the entire region, only then do the fallback behavior?

The reason I think this is useful is because:
1. This behavior would be closer to the vanilla neovim textobject behavior for `ib`/`ab` where "If the cursor is not inside a () block, then find the next '('." 

2. There's some cognitive friction when I encounter an example like the one provided above:
```lua
1    local M = {
2        test = {
3            test2 = { "test" },
4            test3 = { "test" },
..
97           test96 = { "test" }
98       }
99   }
```
Using `search_method='cover_or_next'`, the only ways to select the value of `test` using the `a{` text-object would be to:
1. put the cursor somewhere on line 2 before `{`  and run `van{`
2. put the cursor at the end of line on the `,` on line 3-96, and run `va{`.
3. put the cursor on line 2: `{` or somewhere on line 98,  and run `va{`.
These options work, but are a bit unintuitive and require me to think "oh, I have to select this text-object in a different way than usual". I recognize that this is an edge case that occurs infrequently, but I have indeed encountered it and it does cause some cognitive overhead when it does happen.

Just wondering what your thoughts are on this particular case. Overall mini.nvim has made code editing a much more ergonomic experience for me and I respect your design choices!

> Would you consider adding a config option that forces mini.ai to only search in the entire neighborhood by default, and if no cover region is found in the entire region, only then do the fallback behavior?

I am afraid, this won't be the case at least for the following reasons:
- Although I do find sensible to skip preliminary "next" search in current line before whole neighborhood *in this particular example*, overall experience proved to be less positive (at least for me) in everyday usage. Mostly because covering region is not always so close an obvious and can even be out of screen. So common case of type `i)` and expect to select next visible pair of parenthesis can fail by very unexpectedly selecting much bigger region.
- The 'cover_or_next' search method was mostly a solution to mimic built-in behavior for some of textobjects in absence of "next"/"last" variants which were missing at module's release. They were added slightly later and are a better alternative to an implicit 'cover_or_next' search method (in whichever form it is implemented).
- Selecting covering textobject in presence of "next" on current line can be done by consecutive application in Visual mode: `va}` to start Visual mode and then press `a}` until covering region is selected.

title: [mini.ai] Expect text-object search to `cover`, but instead goes to `next`
